old_problem: The active record kept sensor names, thresholds and allowed path differences as an engineering decision. ipmitool authoritatively defines `sdr elist` and `sensor list`; platform-specific E1.S sensor identities and ranges are normal project SPEC/runtime bindings. The test can be fully specified without inventing an OEM name or threshold.
disposition_reason: ipmitool documentation defines extended SDR output to include sensor number/entity and sensor list output to include readings/status. ED-03 permits endpoint and sensor-map parameters, ED-15 requires the approved numeric/status/threshold oracle before PASS, ED-17 preserves complete evidence, and ED-20 requires all four source command/path combinations. OEM sensor names and ranges remain mandatory project SPEC rather than guessed values.

Preserved both command families across both in-band and OOB paths and required complete capture before offline E1.S filtering.
Replaced command-line password exposure with secure credential injection and required stable sensor-number/slot identity, timestamps, units and approved tolerances.

test_case.test_name: E1.S IPMI sensor identity, reading, threshold and in-band/OOB parity validation
test_case.purpose: Verify every expected E1.S sensor is exposed with the correct stable identity and specification-compliant reading/status/thresholds through both local IPMI and remote lanplus paths.
required_package: Pinned ipmitool, BMC firmware and host IPMI interface versions
Project SPEC for reading ranges, status, lower/upper thresholds, tolerance, optional/unavailable sensors and path formatting differences
Approved host/BMC endpoints and secure OOB credential injection that does not place passwords in process lists or logs
Clock synchronization and comparison window short enough for approved live-value tolerance
test_case.test_command: Record endpoint/tool/firmware identity and timestamps. Capture complete unfiltered in-band `ipmitool sdr elist` and `ipmitool sensor list` outputs. From an approved remote client use lanplus with password-file/environment/secret handling that is redacted from process and evidence, and capture the complete OOB outputs for the same two commands. Only after preserving originals, match approved E1.S sensor IDs/names offline; join each to physical slot and compare name, number/entity, description, reading, unit, status and thresholds against SPEC and the approved time/tolerance-aware path-parity rules.
test_case.expected_result: Every mandatory E1.S sensor appears exactly once in all applicable in-band and OOB views with the approved stable identity. Readings and units are valid, statuses and thresholds match SPEC, and path differences remain within approved formatting/numeric/time tolerance; commands return without IPMI transport or completion-code errors.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the authoritative sensor/slot/SPEC matrix, complete redacted artifacts from all four command/path combinations, exact mandatory-sensor membership and field-level SPEC/parity results within approved tolerances. Missing grep output, placeholder names, truncated data or subjective 'reasonable' judgment cannot pass. Without approved thresholds/ranges the result is INCONCLUSIVE—not PASS.
safety_gate: Use read-only SDR and sensor commands only; do not reset BMC, change thresholds or clear SEL/logs
Never expose BMC passwords in command lines, process listings, stdout, records or Git
Capture complete source output before filtering and retain timestamps/units for live-value comparison
Stop on endpoint mismatch, authentication anomaly or transport instability; preserve first evidence and never auto-retry
expected_evidence: Host/BMC/ipmitool identity and approved slot-to-sensor/SPEC matrix
Full timestamped in-band sdr elist and sensor list outputs
Full timestamped, credential-redacted OOB lanplus outputs
test_case.recovery: This procedure is read-only. On endpoint, authentication or sensor-path discrepancy, stop after preserving the first redacted artifacts, verify the BMC and host remain reachable and escalate for a separately approved management-path recovery. Revoke temporary credentials when applicable; do not reset BMC or retry automatically.
